I have been farming here in the North West for many years, and at 61 I know what works on my land. This bean plot is small—only 0.29 hectares—and beans have always done well enough with the manure I spread from our animals, so I will not spend money on chemical fertilizer this season. But the insects always attack the beans, so I must buy some pesticide to save the crop. My family will do most of the work, though I may hire a few extra hands when the weeding and harvesting are heavy.
